#
# Hash-verified dependency lock for the complete runtime *and* test/dev
# environment, for LINUX (x86_64) -- the platform GitHub Actions and the
# production container both run. Generated inside a python:3.11-slim
# container so the resolution matches that target rather than the
# maintainer's Windows machine:
#
#   docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work:ro -v "$PWD":/out python:3.11-slim bash -c #     'pip install -q pip-tools && cd /work && #      pip-compile --generate-hashes --allow-unsafe --extra dev #        --index-url https://pypi.org/simple #        --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu #        --output-file /out/requirements-lock.txt pyproject.toml'
#
# CPU-only PyTorch, deliberately: this project is CPU-only by design
# (faiss-cpu, and build_serving_context pins torch to a single thread).
# The default Linux torch wheel pulls in the entire CUDA runtime --
# packages a Windows-generated lock never saw, which is exactly what
# made an earlier lock fail hash verification on Linux, plus gigabytes
# of unused supply-chain surface.
#
# Install:
#
#   pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-lock.txt
#   pip install --no-deps -e .
#
--extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
